Name: quality_index_state_specificity
Title: False Alarms Without Contamination: Signal-Quality Indices on an Artifact-Free Simulated EEG Whose Neural State Alone Changes
Short Hypothesis: How large is the false-alarm rate of EEG signal-quality indices on an artifact-free simulated EEG whose neural state alone has changed, and to what dose of contamination is that change equivalent? Although signal-quality indices are read as measures of contamination, we expect a change of neural state of eyes-closed/eyes-open size to raise the false-alarm rate of at least two of three within-recording composite indices, thresholded on the baseline state, to 0.20 or more against a nominal 0.05, because they compare channels and epochs within the recording, which a state change alters. The false-alarm rate is tested on a spiking thalamocortical generator with zero non-neural content and on recorded eyes-closed versus eyes-open rest; the dose that the change equals is only estimated. No simpler route answers it: on recordings state and contamination change together, and only for single-feature spectral indices and a reference-distance index does the direction follow from the definition - those are reported but excluded from the decision.
Related Work: A signal-quality index is read as a measure of non-neural contamination, and clean is defined operationally: the shared denoising benchmark takes ICA-cleaned, visually checked segments as ground-truth clean EEG (Zhang et al., 2021) [zhangetal2021b], and an earlier semi-simulated set uses eyes-closed recordings that were carefully inspected (Klados & Bamidis, 2016) [kladosbamidis2016]. The premise that such scores are specific to contamination is stated and not tested: segments labelled clean are treated as ground truth (Bindra & Panwar, 2026) [bindrapanwar2026], reconstruction scores against them saturate at a few thousand parameters and denoising lowers decoding accuracy on recorded trials (0.643 to 0.597) [bindrapanwar2026], and oracle bounds are computed against the same pool (Shaikh et al., 2026) [shaikhetal2026]. On recordings, data-quality metrics stay associated with a spectral parameter after full ICA cleaning (standardised beta +0.24 to +0.30), and contamination was graded only by swapping recorded segments, with no reference of known content (Troendle & Langer, 2026) [trondlelanger2026]. Quality indices themselves - artifact event duration (Wesierski et al., 2023) [wesierskietal2023], the Riemannian potato field (Barthelemy, 2019) [barthelemy2019], an ensemble for normative resting EEG (Lv et al., 2026) [lvetal2026] - are validated on recordings (abstracts only; their full texts were not obtained). Generators that could supply a signal of known neural origin exist but are not used for this: point-neuron networks with a synaptic-current proxy reproduce a detailed model's EEG with R2 0.94-0.99 against a simulated ground truth (Martinez-Canada et al., 2020) [martinezcanadaetal2020], and a spiking thalamocortical model reaches recorded spindle amplitudes (Rosen et al., 2018) [rosenetal2018]; neither contains artifacts or a quality analysis. A preregistered multi-generator synthetic acquisition-quality benchmark is on record (Choi, 2026) [choi2026] and addresses the contamination side. We found no study that varies neural state at zero contamination and reads quality indices (lookup over all 544 retrieved records; titles and abstracts only). Literature base: 216 screened papers, 27 read in full (plain-text conversion), SEREEGA and the quality-index papers known from abstracts.
Abstract: EEG signal-quality indices are read as measures of non-neural contamination, and the field's definition of a clean signal is a recording after ICA cleaning and inspection. That reading assumes the indices respond to contamination and not to the brain. On recordings the assumption cannot be tested, because neural state and contamination change together - opening the eyes brings blinks, drowsiness brings slow eye movements - and no signal of known neural origin is available; quality metrics have in fact been found to stay associated with spectral parameters after full cleaning. While this is open, a rise in flagged data between conditions, groups or sessions cannot be attributed to the recording or to the brain. We use a spiking thalamocortical generator (Izhikevich simple-model cortex and thalamus, synaptic-current proxy, 68 cortical parcels, BEM lead field, 64 channels) whose output contains no non-neural source. In 24 simulated subjects with individually jittered network parameters we set each index's detection threshold on a separate baseline-state run, then change the neural state alone, by thalamic drive, to an alpha-power change matched to the eyes-closed / eyes-open ratio of a public dataset. Every epoch flagged after that change is a false alarm by construction. The primary test asks whether at least two of three within-recording composite indices (PREP-style, FASTER-style, an invariance-based composite) reach a false-alarm rate of 0.20 against a nominal 0.05; a reference-distance index, whose rise follows from its definition, is reported alongside. Controls give the rate for a second realisation of the baseline state, for a pure gain change, and for planted contamination; the same rate is computed on recordings from eyes-closed thresholds and eyes-open epochs. Separately, recorded ocular and muscle waveforms are added at nine doses to estimate each index's detection curve, the dose that the state change is equivalent to, and whether the changed state masks contamination; a last test asks whether a clean simulated signal outranks recordings. The expected contribution is a false-alarm figure per index, a dose-response map on a signal known to be clean, and an open generator-plus-artifact library for validating quality scores.
Experiments: E0 [instrument] Generator states and decision rules. Run ai_scientist/ideas/clean_eeg_sim (tcx.py one patch; scalp.py 68 Desikan parcels -> fsaverage BEM lead field -> biosemi64, average reference). Each of 24 simulated subjects gets its own connectivity seed and network parameters (synaptic weights, background drives) jittered by 10%. Measure the eyes-closed / eyes-open 8-13 Hz power ratio in ds004148 (60 adults; CC0 per its dataset_description.json, public release for reuse, consent wording not checked beyond the licence file). Scan thalamic background drive (and, if needed, corticothalamic weight) on one patch for a neural state B whose alpha ratio to the baseline state A equals that value. Go/no-go: if the reachable ratio is below half the target in dB, stop and report the generator as unable to make the state change. Conditions per subject, 1-s epochs: a 60-s baseline-state calibration run A0 (thresholds only), a second baseline realisation A' (40 s) and state B (40 s). Write the decision rules of E2-E7 to a file and commit it before any index is computed; fixed before analysis, not externally timestamped. Compute: scan about 15 min; main simulation 24 subjects x 140 s x 68 patches is about 70 CPU-hours, about 5 h on 14 cores (estimated from a timed 1.1 s CPU per simulated second per patch).

E1 [instrument] Signal-quality indices, calibration and unit tests. Seven label-free indices, oriented larger = worse. Within-recording composite set (the decision set): PREP-style percentage of bad channels (robust deviation, correlation, high-frequency noise), FASTER-style composite z, and the Layer-Q composite of EEG_signal_quality_E1_formulas_v2.md. Reported only: Riemannian-potato z-distance (pyriemann 0.12; reference covariance from the calibration run), peak-to-peak rejection rate, mean absolute kurtosis, high-frequency power ratio. Threshold tau_k = 95th percentile of the index over the 60 epochs of the subject's calibration run A0, which is never scored. pyprep and autoreject are not installed today (pure Python, pip-installable): install them and cross-check the PREP-style criteria against pyprep on ds004148 before use. Unit tests: gain and reference invariance where claimed, known values on white noise.

E2 [tests C1] False-alarm rate after a change of neural state alone. For each simulated subject and index, the fraction of the 40 state-B epochs of the artifact-free simulated EEG above tau_k, averaged over subjects per index. FA2 = the second-largest rate among the three within-recording composite indices, with one-sided 95% bootstrap bounds over subjects. Decision rule: supported if the lower bound is at or above 0.20 (at least two indices reach it), refuted if the upper bound is below 0.20, otherwise undecided. Rates for all seven indices, and the rates below the 5th percentile (looks cleaner), are reported. No new simulation.

E3 [control C1] Negative control and nuisance arms. The second baseline realisation A' is scored in place of B: expected false-alarm rate 0.05 per index; E2 is read only if every decision index's mean rate on A' lies within 0.05 +/- 0.03. Also scored: the baseline signal scaled to the RMS of B (gain only), state B rescaled to the RMS of A, and both states after an 18-22 Hz notch, with the power of the generator's 20 Hz harmonic reported per state. No new simulation.

E4 [control C1] Positive control. Half of the A' epochs are replaced by baseline epochs with ocular or muscle contamination at a dose where E5 shows the detection rate has saturated: expected rate per index, and hence FA2, = 0.5 x 1 + 0.5 x 0.05 = 0.525 (at a detection rate p: 0.5 p + 0.025); this control can be read only after E5 has located a saturated dose for each decision index. No new simulation.

E5 [descriptive C2] Dose-response on a signal known to be clean. Contamination library: ocular and muscle waveforms from ds003478 (30 adults, rest with EOG channels; CC0 per its dataset_description.json, consent wording not checked beyond the licence file) as EOG-locked sensor patterns, and from the phantom-head dataset ds004784 (CC0; no human subject); synthetic 50 Hz line and electrode pops. Doses a in {0, 0.03, 0.06, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1}, a = 1 being the amplitude as recorded relative to the background of the source recording, added at the sensors to A' and B. Per index and class: detection rate per dose, smallest dose with detection rate 0.5, the state-equivalent dose (whose detection rate equals the state-B false-alarm rate), and the change of detection rate between states (masking); median and interquartile range over subjects. Minutes on CPU (estimated).

E6 [tests C1] The false-alarm rate on recordings. In ds004148, thresholds from the first half of each subject's eyes-closed epochs; flagged fraction of eyes-open epochs without a detected ocular event (EOG or frontal-amplitude criterion) and of held-out eyes-closed epochs (expected 0.05). Same indices and statistic (second-largest of the three within-recording rates) over 60 subjects. Refuted-if: E2 is supported but the upper one-sided 95% bound of the eyes-open false-alarm rate is below 0.20 - the simulated result is then not taken to hold for recorded EEG. The recorded rate is an upper bound on the state effect, because eyes-open epochs can hold undetected ocular activity. Under an hour on CPU (estimated).

E7 [tests C3] Does a clean simulated signal outrank recordings? Claim tested: at least one index calibrated on recordings rates the artifact-free simulated EEG worse than the median recording. Calibrate the reference-based indices on half of the ds004148 eyes-closed recordings, score the other half and the 24 simulated subjects (clean). The claim is refuted if every reference-calibrated index rates the simulated EEG better than the median recording (one-sided Mann-Whitney, alpha = 0.05, Holm-corrected). Positive control: simulated EEG with contamination at a = 1 must score worse than clean simulated EEG. Minutes (estimated).
E8 [release] Package the generator states, the contamination library with its dose scale, the index code with unit tests and the per-index tables.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Blind restatement unresolved: a supported result may be a property of the generator, and E6 can veto but not corroborate it - no recording on this machine has a change of neural state with independently verified zero contamination (the phantom ds004784 has no neural state; eyes-open epochs of ds004148 can hold undetected ocular activity).

Blind restatement unresolved: the 24 simulated subjects are jittered copies of one network, not between-person variability, and the 0.20 cut-off is a design choice - no measured between-person distribution of this generator's parameters exists to sample from.

Blind restatement unresolved: the equivalent dose is expressed on a scale tied to two source datasets, and the positive control depends on E5 finding a saturated dose - no artifact library on this machine has a dose scale independent of its source recording.

Coherence unresolved: the primary claim was not restated after the forced revision (the decision set changed from four composite indices to three within-recording indices, and thresholds moved to a separate calibration run).
Question narrowed from: How much do EEG signal-quality indices change when the neural state of an artifact-free simulated EEG changes, relative to their change under a known dose of contamination?
Decision rules not externally timestamped: they are fixed in a local commit before analysis; a third party can check the commit order but not its date.
Detection floors and equivalent doses (C2) are in the units of a dose scale tied to two source datasets; this bias is not addressed.
If the simulated EEG scores worse than recordings (C3), generator defects that resemble contamination (the 20 Hz harmonic) cannot be separated from atypicality; not addressed.

The result holds for one generator, one state path (thalamic drive), thresholds calibrated on the baseline state and three within-recording indices; it does not cover sleep or drug states, classifier-based quality indices, other generators, or thresholds calibrated across states (where the rate is bounded near nominal by construction).

For the single-feature spectral indices and the Riemannian-potato distance the direction of the shift follows from the definition; they are reported but carry no decision. The because clause (comparison within the recording) is a conjecture.
Compute: the main simulation is about 5 h on 14 cores, estimated from a timed rate, not timed in full.

Power: 24 simulated subjects detect a standardized difference of 0.51 or more (80% power, one-sided); no literature value exists for this false-alarm rate, so the verdict is marginal and 'undecided' is a possible outcome. The same holds for C3 (24 simulated vs 60 recorded).
The primary claim is one-sided (flagged as worse); masking of contamination by the changed state is estimated, not tested.
No positive result on recordings can confirm the simulated one: in E6 eyes-open epochs may hold undetected ocular activity, so the recorded rate is an upper bound.
Significance not supported by the literature: whether quality-based exclusion selects on the neural variable under study; the warrant of C3 also has no literature basis.
The generator may not reach the eyes-closed / eyes-open alpha ratio by thalamic drive alone (go/no-go in E0).
Identical cortical patches, no cortico-cortical coupling and a flat aperiodic slope make the simulated state change unlike a recorded one.
The FASTER-style and Layer-Q indices are own implementations without a reference implementation to check against; only the PREP-style criteria are cross-checked (pyprep).
Literature base: 27 of 216 screened papers read in full, as plain text; quality-index papers and SEREEGA known from abstracts only; Semantic Scholar was rate-limited during search and snowball.
